paragraphs: Blocksi sells internet content filtering, classroom screen monitoring and student safety software to K-12 school districts. Its filtering covers YouTube and the web and is built for K-12 teachers and students.

A safety layer runs around the clock, watching for early signs of a threat. The company presents its classroom tool as more than a screen monitoring system. The stated mission is to give schools full control over internet content and student devices.

Blocksi, Inc. says it was established in 2011 and is headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Its team brings together K-12 education professionals, former educators, and IT experts. The company dates its first customer to 2014 and its cloud-based market entry to 2015. It claims more than 500 school districts and 3 million users. Growth after the pandemic, it says, was strongest in North America, South America, Europe, and Asia.
